pages.hook: In many American cities, people give directions with blocks, traffic lights and left or right turns. A short answer with two or three steps is usually enough.
pages.polite: Finish with **“You can’t miss it!”** to tell the person the place is easy to see.

mythfact.s: In Manhattan, streets run east-west and avenues run north-south.
mythfact.why: This grid helps people find addresses quickly.

mythfact.s: Boston has only straight, new streets.
mythfact.why: Boston is old and many of its streets are narrow and curved.

mythfact.s: A “block” is the distance from one street to the next.
Pedestrians must cross when the signal says “Don’t Walk”.
mythfact.why: Wait for the “Walk” signal to cross safely.

lines: Turn left at the traffic light.

compare.br: In Brazil people often say “segue reto” and use landmarks like a bakery, a church or a gas station.
compare.us: In the USA people also count blocks and say “turn left at the light”.
compare.tip: Say the steps in order: straight, turn, walk one more block.

quiz.q: When you say “You can’t miss it”, you mean…
quiz.why: It is very easy to find.

pages.title: Reading quest — A walk to the museum in Boston
text: On my second day in Boston, I wanted to see a museum. I was near a park, and I saw a woman with a coffee. “**Excuse me, how do I get to the museum?**” I asked.
“**Go straight for two blocks**,” she said. I repeated, “Two blocks, then?” She smiled. “**Turn left at the traffic light**.” “And then?” I asked. “**Walk one more block. It’s on your right**.”
I asked, “Is it a big building?” “**Yes, with a red door**,” she said. “**Good luck! You can’t miss it**.” I said thanks and started to walk. The sun was warm, and the streets were quiet.
I counted: one block, two blocks. At the corner, there was a traffic light, and it was red. I waited. When it turned green, I crossed and turned left. I walked one more block and looked to my right.
There it was! A tall brick building with a big red door. The woman was right: I could not miss it. I felt proud because I understood the directions in English.
Next time, I will ask more questions and use my phone less. People are friendly, and a short conversation can be the best map.
